explanation: Requested kinematics (eta production, W=1.7 GeV, Q2=-0.5 GeV^2, cos theta*=0, phi*=90 deg) are physically impossible: Q^2 = -q^2 = 4*E*E'*sin^2(theta_e/2) is by definition non-negative for single-virtual-photon electroproduction (ep -> e'p eta). Q^2 < 0 would require a timelike exchanged photon, which does not occur in this process; there is no electron beam energy / scattering angle combination that produces Q^2 = -0.5 GeV^2. This is confirmed by the kinematics routines in eta/exclurad.F: cthe = 1 - Q2/(2*bmom*bmom_prime) (exclurad.F line ~306) gives cos(theta_e) > 1 for negative Q2, i.e. no real scattering angle exists, and eps_d = 1/(1+2*(1+nu^2/Q2)*tan^2(theta_e/2)) (line ~308) divides by a negative Q2, producing a non-physical virtual-photon polarization. W=1.7 GeV is fine (above the eta-p threshold of ~1.486 GeV) and cos(theta*)=0, phi*=90 are valid angular inputs, but the negative Q2 value alone makes the point unphysical, so no input.dat was generated. To proceed, provide a positive Q2 (e.g. Q2=0.5 GeV^2 if the sign was a typo), or clarify if a different variable (e.g. Mandelstam t, which can be negative) was intended.
